title: Safemode cluster init and drift scenarios (playbook notes)
content:
Purpose
Keep a short, pragmatic playbook sketch for: bootstrapping clusters in SAFEMODE (low-impact), handling accidental config drift detected post-provision, plus terraform module notes and an upgrade/rollback rehearsal plan. This is a working note for field engineers and SREs preparing private (VPC/on-prem) deployments that combine bare metal and vSphere.

Scope and assumptions
- Target: on-prem clusters used for Redwood Private customer installs (airgapped and connected).
- We assume hardware inventory and BMC/IPMI access is available for bootstrap nodes.
- Primary installer: kubeadm + k0s minimal for deterministic control-plane init (team decided k0s later, but sketches here are kubeadm-compatible).
- Network: immutable-control-plane network ranges are pre-allocated by infra; DHCP reserved for ephemeral workers.
- Terraform is the source-of-truth for host objects (ipmi creds, VLAN tags, hostnames). We must minimize manual changes after apply.

High-level goals
- An init path ("safemode") that leaves user workloads offline until post-validation action. Useful for airgap where first bootstrap must be verified offline.
- Detect accidental drift (e.g., manual IP change, VLAN tagging, OS reimage) and provide clear remediation steps that prefer automated reconciliation (terraform) when safe.
- Upgrade plan that can be rehearsed in staging and supports canary control-plane swaps.

Safemode bootstrap sequence (operational checklist, minimal):
1) Preflight (local laptop / ops jump host)
   - Confirm artifact repo is reachable (for connected installs) or local repo is built and verified (airgap).
   - Validate NTP/chrony on all hosts (time skew > 500ms -> fail).
   - Ensure KMS/HSM reachability for customer-managed keys (if enabled).
   - Verify terraform state backend (s3/consul) connectivity and lock acquisition.

2) Terraform apply (control-plane and host objects only)
   - terraform init
   - terraform plan -var-file=site-vars.tfvars -out=plan.out
   - terraform apply plan.out
   Notes: use -target sparingly. For safemode, apply control-plane nodes + ipmi secrets, do NOT apply worker pools.

3) Bootstrap control-plane nodes (one at a time)
   - PXE/iso -> provisioning -> OS hardening -> sysctl/NIC config per site profile.
   - kubeadm init --control-plane-endpoint=lb.example.local --upload-certs --pod-network-cidr=10.244.0.0/16  (replace with k0s/kubeadm equivalent).
   - Mark cluster as SAFEMODE: add label redwood/boot-mode=safemode to cluster config map.
   - Do smoke checks: etcd health, apiserver responding, core DNS stub, certs present.

4) Post-init validations (must pass before enabling workers)
   - etcd snapshot saved to objstore and verified (run 'etcdctl snapshot status').
   - RBAC default tokens rotated and stored in vault.
   - Firewall rules audited: control-plane only ports open from jump/CIDR.

5) Approve worker pool rollouts (manual gate)
   - When safemode validations green, toggle terraform to apply worker pools and autoscaler policies.
   - Run canary workloads with limits (cpu=10m, mem=32Mi) and validate scheduling and network policies.

Accidental drift detection and remediation notes
- Detection channels:
  - Terraform plan nightly job (compare remote state to desired) -> alert on >1 diff
  - kubelet/cni mismatch metric (node-not-ready due to network config)
  - Inventory agent heartbeat (IP/hostname mismatch)
  - BMC health change notifications

- Example drift scenarios and playbook actions:
  A) Manual IP reconfiguration on host
    - Symptoms: terraform plan shows host.ip != state; node still present but kubelet registers with old IP.
    - Immediate: isolate host (cordon + drain if possible), do not reassign workloads until reconciliation.
    - Remediation path 1 (automated-safe): run terraform apply to update host object and trigger control-plane to re-register. If kubelet certificate IP SAN mismatch occurs, rotate node cert via rotation job.
    - Remediation path 2 (manual and safer): reprovision host via PXE using the immutable image and re-run bootstrap steps.

  B) VLAN tag changed in switch config (networking drift)
    - Symptoms: multiple nodes NotReady, sudden pod traffic drops.
    - Immediate: open incident channel, add tag to incident doc. Verify switch change; if accidental, roll back switch change with network team.
    - Terraform cannot revert switch-level config (out-of-band). Add network-device change to linked_artifacts and require a ticket for future terraform integration.

  C) Accidental OS package update on control-plane
    - Symptoms: etcd or kubelet service failure after unattended package update.
    - Immediate: Promote etcd leader to standby if possible, restore etcd snapshot, spin new control-plane from image pinned in repo.
    - Rollback: If update is reversible, perform apt/dnf history rollback; otherwise reprovision node and rejoin.

Terraform module notes (practical pointers)
- Keep host-level secrets out of main modules; pass in secret_id references. Use a small "host-provision" module with explicit outputs: ipmi_address, provisioning_iso, facility_tag.
- Module variables to prefer: host_role (control|worker|bootstrap), rack_id, bios_profile, network_profile. Avoid baking site-specific CIDR into modules; use site overlay tfvars.
- State handling: control-plane state should be isolated (state file per-site-controlplane.tfstate) to reduce blast radius for terraform state locks.
- Recommended provider versions and pinning: include provider constraints in registry.tf to prevent drift from provider SDK changes.
- Testing: add a lightweight "terraform validate + terratest" job in CI that applies a small ephemeral plan in a nested virtualization environment.

Upgrade & rollback rehearsal plan (control-plane first)
- Objectives: upgrade from k8s X -> X+2 with minimal downtime, verify certificate rotations, and validate node kubelet ABI compatibility.

1) Pre-upgrade gating
   - Verify e2e smoke tests passing on staging (apiserver, controller-manager, scheduler, coreDNS, ingress).
   - Confirm third-party CRDs compatible with target version (crd-version-checker job).
   - Take etcd snapshot and upload to secure storage.

2) Canary control-plane node upgrade
   - Drain control-plane? No. Instead add new control-plane node with upgraded kubelet/ctrl-plane binaries, join, then remove the oldest. This reduces leader-flapping.
   - Validate etcd quorum with new binary. Run read/write test across endpoints.

3) Worker rolling upgrade
   - Use node-pool with maxUnavailable=1 and a low surge for canaries. Deploy a diagnostic daemonset that reports kernel/rt/selinux differences post-upgrade.

4) Post-upgrade validations
   - Run heavy workload smoke: simple request/response latency tests, e2e CI on representative apps, integration tests for networkpolicy and ingress.

5) Rollback options
   - Fastest: revert terraform to previous image and re-provision failed nodes (worker reprovisioning is cheap).
   - Control-plane rollback: restore etcd snapshot to a pre-upgrade cluster only if cluster is irreparably degraded. This is high-risk and requires coordination with ownership and a maintenance window.

Operational runbook snippets and quick commands
- terraform plan diff to find drift: terraform plan -var-file=site.tfvars -refresh=true -detailed-exitcode || true
- Save etcd snapshot: ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl snapshot save /tmp/snap.db --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 --cacert=/etc/etcd/ca.crt --cert=/etc/etcd/peer.crt --key=/etc/etcd/peer.key
- Check kube-apiserver: kubectl get --raw='/healthz?verbose' | jq .checks
- Rotate kubelet cert: TODO: add the wrapper command we use in the field (depends on distro).

Tests and rehearsal matrix (short)
- Preflight scenarios (automated): state-backend-unreachable, time-skew, missing-artifact, ipmi-failure.
- Failover rehearsals (manual): etcd leader loss, control-plane node reboot storm, partial network outage between racks.
- Drift experiments (staging): change host ip, reimage worker with different kernel, change MTU on switch ports. Confirm detection and remediation flows fire.

Airgap-specific considerations
- Build and validate a local YUM/APT repo mirror, container registry mirror, and image bundle (tarball of images + manifest).
- Artifact signing: all images and packages signed; bootstrap verifies signatures against local keyring.
- Time sync: NTP fallback to internal stratum or GPS; explain how to handle leap-second differences.

Open questions / TODOs
- Decide on formal naming for SAFEMODE flag in cluster annotations and where it is surfaced in Console.
- Flesh out node-certificate rotation tooling (Samir owns an epic).
- Integrate network-device change detection into Terraform drift alerts (we need a mapping from device configs to TF resources).
- Add automated reconcilers for minor drift: e.g., ip address drift that only requires kubelet restart vs full reprovision.

References & incident links
- Jira: INF-1287 (safemode bootstrap prototype)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules/pull/342 (host-provision refactor)
- Slack: #private-deployments (search thread "safemode init")

Notes to self
- Keep this doc lean; convert to a proper runbook when we land the safemode gate UI and the terraform module refactor.
- When testing, explicitly record the terraform state lock acquisition timings (we hit >30s locks in lab during large plans).
- Plan a drill: run a "control-plane upgrade rehearsal" in staging on 2025-12-08.
summary: Draft playbook for an immutable safemode bootstrap, drift detection & remediation patterns, terraform module guidance, and an upgrade/rollback rehearsal plan for on-prem Kubernetes clusters (bare metal + vSphere).
